what_it_does: Verilog is a programming language used to describe the behavior of computer chips before they are manufactured; bugs in a Verilog design can cause expensive chip failures. Finding the exact line of code responsible for a bug — called bug localization — currently requires either human experts or automated tools built by experts, and existing automated methods can only narrow bugs down to a set of suspicious lines rather than pinpointing one. This paper presents LiK (Location is Key), a large language model (LLM — an AI system trained on massive amounts of text that can read and generate code) specifically fine-tuned for Verilog bug localization. LiK starts from a general-purpose code LLM (Deepseek-Coder), then goes through three training stages: continued pre-training on Verilog code to build domain knowledge, supervised fine-tuning on examples of bug localization to teach the specific task, and reinforcement learning (a feedback-driven training loop) to further reduce mistakes. Based on the abstract alone, the exact accuracy and benchmark comparisons are not confirmed.
